title: Modern Defense: the ideas
line: The bishop goes to the long diagonal at once, and Black keeps the knights home to stay flexible.

steps.text: White starts by pushing the pawn in front of its king two squares, into the center.
Push the pawn on g7 one square, to make room for your bishop.

also.e7e5: That is the open game, another main answer. This lesson goes on with the Modern.
also.c7c5: That is the Sicilian Defense, another main answer. This lesson goes on with the Modern.
also.e7e6: That is the French Defense, another main answer. This lesson goes on with the Modern.

steps.text: Put the bishop on g7. It aims at the pawn on d4.

also.d7d6: That also works, and can turn into the Pirc. This lesson brings the bishop out first.
also.c7c6: That also works. This lesson brings the bishop out first.

steps.after: Black lets White build a full center for now, to attack it later. White gets space; Black gets targets.

steps.text: Push the pawn on d7 one square. It keeps White's pawn out of e5.

also.d7d5: That is also played. This lesson pushes the pawn one square.
also.c7c6: That also works. This lesson pushes the pawn in front of the queen.

steps.text: Push the pawn on a7 one square. It gets ready to push the pawn on b7.

also.c7c6: That also works. This lesson goes on with the other side pawn.
also.g8f6: That turns into the Pirc. This lesson goes on with the side pawn.

steps.text: Push the pawn on b7 two squares. It takes space on the queen's side.
Bring the knight to d7. It backs up a push in the center.
Bring the other bishop out. It aims at the pawn on e4.
Now strike at the center: push the pawn on c7 two squares.
steps.after: Your pawn hits d4, and your bishops aim at the center from both sides.

summary: The Modern puts a bishop on the long diagonal at once, takes space on the queen's side and strikes at the center later.
